visualSourcesReviewed.observations: The pinned image shows a Cartesian grid with axes, a sin(x) expression in a left expression panel, and a 6-unit vertical scale marker in the visible graph. It is a Desmos reference screenshot, not retained evidence of the implementation at desktop or tablet widths.

The pinned Story's circle requirement is test-oriented, while the evidence file has only a passing Playwright/Vitest name claiming circle geometry.

rows.note: The verification evidence does not provide the separate visual inspection required by the plan. It instead marks AC-004 verified even though the plan names visual inspection and marks no tagged test.

findings.message: Generation 5 marks D-STORY:AC-004 verified and recommends release, but its own evidence table says “no tagged test”; the specification and plan require representative desktop/tablet visual inspection. The pinned image is a Desmos reference, not a capture of this implementation. How could this pass be claimed without actual implementation desktop/tablet evidence?

The verification artifact recommends release on the basis of “9 of 10 requirements verified,” while AC-004 has no test or visual evidence. This is a material inconsistency between the retained evidence and the result because a required width/visibility clause is marked verified without proof.
